name: Banjara Camp & Retreat Sangla
why_it_matters: Captain G.S. Sood's 1994 camp on the Baspa River at Batseri village (5km from Sangla bazaar) is the Baspa valley's defining property — a riverside apple-orchard set-up where dinner is barbecued trout and a bonfire. The kitchen pioneered Sangla's hospitality scene.
insider_tip: Day-trippers can call ahead to book lunch — non-residents are accommodated when capacity allows. Trout is the order; everything else is competent but the BBQ is what they built the property around.
signature_address: Banjara Camp & Retreat, Batseri, Sangla Valley, Kinnaur 172106

name: Kinner Camp Sangla
why_it_matters: Long-running tented camp on the slope above Sangla — the buffet-style dining hall is the kitchen most consistently praised on TripAdvisor for the valley. Tulsi, the dining in-charge, gets named in review after review.
insider_tip: Three buffet windows only — breakfast 8-9:30am, lunch 1-2:30pm, dinner 8-9:30pm. Show up outside those slots and you're on chai-and-biscuits. Locally-pressed apple juice is offered at no extra charge in season.

name: Hotel Mount Kailash
must_try: garden salad from on-site organic patch
why_it_matters: Family-run hotel near Sangla main market with the broadest non-camp menu in the bazaar — Indian, tandoori, Chinese and Italian. Their organic kitchen garden supplies salad and herb produce, which is rare for the valley.
insider_tip: Indoor or terrace seating, your call — terrace gets the Kinnaur range view but goes cold by 7pm. The tandoor is fired only for dinner; lunch is gas-stove cooking, so plan accordingly.

name: Chang Saaring Cafe
why_it_matters: One of only three standalone restaurants TripAdvisor lists in Sangla — a small Chinese-leaning cafe with a perfect 5/5 review pattern from the handful who've left feedback. The mountain view is the actual draw.
insider_tip: Closed in winter (Nov–Mar); open seasonally. Phone ahead — one bad-weather day shutters the place without notice. Cash only.
